title: Open Observability Results Standard (OORS)
description: A lightweight, tool-agnostic format to exchange data quality and data observability results.

apiVersion.description: Version of the OORS schema used. Indicates the version of the standard, e.g., `v0.8.1`.

kind.description: The type of OORS object. For OORS, always `ObservabilityResults`.

id.description: A unique identifier (could be a UUID) identifying the specific observability results.

observedAt.description: The moment in time when the observations were done (ISO 8601 format).

source.description: Object describing the source from where the results come (e.g., job, pipeline, etc.).

process.description: The name of the process (job, pipeline, etc.) that made the observations.

runId.description: An optional unique identifier for the specific run/execution of the process (e.g., build ID, run ID, etc.).

vendor.description: An optional field indicating the vendor or tool that produced the observations (e.g., `soda`, `dbt`, `inhouse-build`, etc.).

run.description: Optional run lifecycle object. When absent, the document is terminal: the authoritative record of a run. When present with `state: running`, the document is an interim snapshot of a run still in progress.

state.description: The lifecycle state of the run this document reports on. `running`: interim snapshot, more documents will follow for this `source.runId`. `completed`: terminal, the run finished and this document is its authoritative record. `aborted`: terminal, the run ended before producing its full results.

startedAt.description: Optional moment in time when the run started (ISO 8601 format). Together with `observedAt`, it gives the duration of the run.

sequence.description: Optional monotonically increasing ordinal of this document within the run (per `source.runId`). Consumers SHOULD order documents by `sequence` when present, falling back to `observedAt`.

progress.description: Optional progress indicator for the run.

current.description: The amount of progress made so far, e.g., steps completed.

total.description: Optional total amount expected, e.g., total steps. Omit when unknown.

contract.description: Object describing the contract that provided the specifications for the observations. Optional but highly recommended for traceability and context. When provided, all observations in `results` are expected to be based on the specifications defined in that contract.

contractId.description: A unique identifier (could be a UUID) identifying the specific contract (ODCS/ODPS) that provided the specifications for the observations.

standard.description: The standard followed by the contract, e.g., `ODCS`, `ODPS`, etc.

version.description: The version of the contract (not the standard), e.g., `1.0.0`, `2.0.0`, etc.

server.description: The identifier of the server, as defined in the referenced contract (e.g., the `server` name in the ODCS `servers` section), against which the observations were made, e.g., `production`. A contract can be served on multiple servers; this field records which one the results apply to.

results.description: An array of results. Each result object carries the details of a specific observation (check or metric). May be empty when the run made no observations, e.g. no checks were defined or all were filtered out.

status.description: Optional overall outcome of the observations in this document, so consumers do not need to aggregate `results` themselves. When present, it SHOULD equal the outcome derived from `results`: the first of `error`, `fail`, `warn`, `pass`, `skip` that occurs as a result status, or `unknown` when none does (including when `results` is empty). On an interim snapshot (`run.state: running`), it covers only the results reported so far.

Result.description: A single result object carrying the details of a specific observation.

id.description: A unique identifier for the specific check/metric.

type.description: The type of observation: `check` (for pass/fail checks) or `metric` (for measured values).

name.description: A human-readable name for the check/metric.

status.description: The outcome of the observation: `pass` (executed, met expectation), `fail` (executed, breached a hard threshold), `warn` (executed, breached a soft/warning threshold), `error` (could not be evaluated - verdict unknown; e.g. the query failed or the source was unreachable), `skip` (intentionally not run), or `unknown` (the producer cannot tell the outcome; e.g. it relays a result from another tool whose status it does not recognize). `error` is distinct from `fail`: a failure is a known-bad verdict, an error is the absence of a verdict and must not be counted as a failure. `unknown` is distinct from `error`: nothing broke that needs fixing, and it must be counted neither as a pass nor as a failure.

relatesTo.description: Optional reference to the element this result relates to in the linked contract, e.g., a path to a data quality rule or property in the ODCS/ODPS contract referenced by the top-level `contract` object.

severity.description: The severity level of the observation, e.g., `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `warning`, etc. Severity is orthogonal to `status`: `status` is the runtime outcome, `severity` is the definition-time importance of the check.

dimension.description: The dimension of data quality being observed, e.g., `accuracy`, `completeness`, `consistency`, `timeliness`, `validity`, `uniqueness`, etc. (following ODCS data quality dimensions).

target.description: Object describing the resource being observed.

resourceType.description: The type of resource, e.g., `table`, `column`, `dataset`, etc.

resourceIdentifier.description: The identifier(s) of the resource, e.g., table name, column name, etc. May be a single string or an array of strings.

filter.description: Optional condition that restricted the observed data to a subset of the resource, e.g., a partition or a where clause such as `order_date >= '2026-10-01'`. When present, the result applies only to that subset, not to the whole resource.

metric.description: The name of the metric being measured, e.g., `rowCount`, `age`, `latency`, etc. For data quality metrics, use the ODCS library metric names where one applies: `rowCount`, `nullValues`, `missingValues`, `invalidValues`, `duplicateValues`.

value.description: The observed value of the metric.

threshold.description: Object describing the threshold criteria, e.g., `mustBe`, `mustBeLowerOrEqual`, etc. (following ODCS operator definitions).

unit.description: The unit of measurement, e.g., `rows`, `seconds`, `percent`, etc.

rowCount.description: Optional number of rows the observation evaluated.

failedRowCount.description: Optional number of evaluated rows that did not meet the expectation. Together with `rowCount`, it gives the share of failing rows, independent of the metric in `value`.

message.description: A human-readable message providing additional context about the observation.

CustomProperties.description: A list of key/value pairs for custom properties. Shared structure across the Bitol standards.

property.description: The name of the key. Names should be in camel case—the same as if they were permanent properties in the standard.

description.description: Optional description of the custom property.

id.description: Optional unique identifier for the custom property, for stable references.

vendor.description: Identifies the vendor, provider, or external system associated with this custom property. SHOULD be a stable, lowercase identifier matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ (e.g. confluent, zeenea, atlan, soda). Tools MUST preserve unknown vendor values.

Tags.description: A list of tags that may be assigned to the elements (object or property); the tags keyword may appear at any level. Tags may be used to better categorize an element. For example, `finance`, `sensitive`, `employee_record`.
